newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Howard mulls "pair" on Colston.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Howard mulls "pair" on Colston.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Monday the government would have to consider a temporary adjustment to Senate voting if senator Mal Colston, accused of fraud, were to leave the upper house.
"If a vacancy occurs, and that includes a vacancy created by him or indeed any other senator going, then obviously we would have to give attention to the question of pairing," Howard said.
"Pairing" is the voluntary abstention from parliamentary voting by a member of one party to offset the absence of a member of the opposing party.
The understanding, intended to maintain the balance of power, is most commonly arranged to allow members of parliament to attend important functions.
But each of the main parties grants "a pair" to the other to avoid exploiting unfortunate circumstances, such as a death.
Howard said a pair had been granted in the 1980s when a senator left parliament.

Colston, who denies all allegations against him, has been accused in a government administrative tribunal of misusing expense allowances and of giving office jobs to relatives who did not actually work.
The Administrative Affairs Department is investigating possible irregularities in his use of several entitlements.
Colston has not been charged with any offence.
